name: BIRTH WORK Azabu-Juban
card: Floors split into “focus” and “relax”, with a wall of timber shelves downstairs
title: BIRTH WORK Azabu-Juban — a shared office one minute from the station, with a 5th floor for focus and 8th–9th floors to relax
lead: BIRTH WORK Azabu-Juban is in the Azabu-Juban Takagi Building, a one-minute walk from Azabu-Juban Station. The 5th floor is for focus and the 8th and 9th floors are for relaxing, and it is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. On the ground and basement floors of the same building is BIRTH LAB, known for its wall of timber shelves. It is run by Takagi Building Co., Ltd. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open every day (except building inspections), 24-hour access
hero_cap: BIRTH WORK in the Azabu-Juban Takagi Building
concept: Where the seeds of an idea sprout and grow

BIRTH WORK describes itself as “the place where the seeds of an idea sprout and begin to grow”. BIRTH is a brand of Takagi Building, with sites in Azabu-Juban, Kanda and Toranomon, a community space called BIRTH LAB and a membership called BIRTHERs.

In Azabu-Juban, each floor has a role: the 5th is for focus, the 8th and 9th for relaxing. BIRTH LAB, a community space open to the neighbourhood, sits on the lower floors — stacking a place to work and a place to gather in the same building.
steps: The 5th floor is for focus, and the private desks are here too.
Non-members can drop in for ¥660 an hour or ¥2,420 for a day pass (both 10:00–18:00).
Floors for working at an easier pace
The 8th and 9th floors are for relaxing, and private offices are on these two floors.
BIRTHERs monthly membership is ¥38,500 a month (sign-up fee ¥16,500), with access 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
A wall of timber shelves, one space from B1 to 2F

The website describes BIRTH LAB as “featuring timber shelves that project across an entire wall, with high ceilings, B1 to 2F forming a single space”. It has a studio on the ground floor, street-side terrace seats, a lounge on the 2nd floor and a kitchen half a floor down.
Each floor can be rented by the hour, or the whole building booked out. It is where neighbours and people working in the building meet.
BIRTH LAB studio — a wall of timber shelves

word.title: What are BIRTHERs?
body: The name for BIRTH's monthly members. In Azabu-Juban it costs ¥38,500 a month for 24/7 access to the workspace.
Members are called companions who grow the place together, not people who rent a desk — the name says a lot about how it is run.

name: 3×3Lab Future
card: Bamboo desks, cedar floors, traditional joinery — an Otemachi third place that speaks through materials
title: 3×3Lab Future — 11 zones built from Japanese timber and green technology, on the ground floor of Otemon Tower ENEOS Building
lead: About two minutes' walk from Otemachi Station, 3×3Lab Future (pronounced “san-san lab future”) is on the ground floor of Otemon Tower ENEOS Building. Its name combines the three elements of sustainability — society, environment and economy — with the idea of a “third place” that is neither home nor office. It is made up of 11 zones in which every material carries a meaning: desks of laminated bamboo, floors of Japanese cedar, a room built with traditional itakura joinery. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 11 zones (Salon, Future Café, Garden of Light and more)
hero_cap: The Salon — laminated-bamboo desks and chairs on a sisal floor
concept: A third place where society, environment and economy mesh like gears

3×3Lab Future aims to be a hub for exchange and activity across industries, where the three elements of sustainability — society, environment and economy — mesh like gears, and which serves as a third place, neither office nor home. It is run by the Ecozzeria Association, and Mitsubishi Estate positions it as a platform for creating CSV businesses.

The interior turns its materials into a message about the environment: mortise-and-tenon desks and chairs of laminated bamboo from Kurashiki, Okayama; a floor of leftover chopstick offcuts; cedar flooring reused from construction scaffolding boards; cubes of fragrant Owase cedar. Each zone notes where its materials came from.
steps: A floor you can walk on barefoot, for seminars of 120
The Salon can host seminars for 120 people. Its 100% sisal floor feels good underfoot, and the raised veranda at the front hides storage beneath.
The desks and chairs come from a laminated-bamboo project in Kurashiki, Okayama, and are made with mortise-and-tenon joints, a traditional Japanese woodworking technique.
The Salon — laminated-bamboo desks and chairs on a sisal floor
120 m² of cedar reused from scaffolding
The communication zone is a 120 m² space for many kinds of gatherings. Movable tables, sofas and partitions that double as decor let the space change.
The floor is Japanese cedar reused from construction scaffolding boards. The neighbouring Future Café can become a half-enclosed meeting room or a kitchen for events.
03 · Garden of Light and reception room
A courtyard of mixed trees and a room in traditional joinery
The Garden of Light is a “courtyard of diversity” mixing broadleaf and coniferous trees, with LED lighting and automatic watering.

The reception room recreates the itakura construction method under the supervision of Kunihiro Ando, professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba. The painting on the wall is “Big Bang” by yuzen dyeing artist Yuki Nagatomo.
The reception room, built with itakura joinery
A small meeting room with an offcut floor, and a kitchen to gather around
The CO2 room is an eco-conscious small meeting room with LED-integrated radiant panels, a floor of chopstick offcuts and single-material chairs that are easy to recycle.
The workshop kitchen can be used for cooking, sharing a table or events, with a meeting area that can be partitioned off.

word.title: What is itakura construction?
body: A traditional Japanese way of building in wood, where thick boards are slotted between posts to form the walls. The reception room at 3×3Lab Future recreates it under the supervision of professor emeritus Kunihiro Ando.
A room built with traditional joinery on the ground floor of an office tower — a rare chance to experience Japanese timber construction in the middle of the business district.

credits: 3×3Lab Future official website: “About”; Mitsubishi Estate: “3×3Lab Future”; Ecozzeria: “Access”

name: Global Business Hub Tokyo
card: 50 furnished offices on one floor of Otemachi Financial City
title: Global Business Hub Tokyo — a shared office linking Otemachi and the world, on the 3rd floor of Otemachi Financial City Grand Cube
lead: Global Business Hub Tokyo, run by Mitsubishi Estate, is on the 3rd floor of Otemachi Financial City Grand Cube. It has 50 furnished offices for 2–20 people, 14 meeting rooms for 4–20 and an event space for up to 200, all available 24 hours. It is built for overseas companies entering Japan and for Japanese companies aiming at the world. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 50 furnished offices (2–20 people) / 14 meeting rooms (4–20) / event space (up to 200)
hero_cap: The floor at Global Business Hub Tokyo
concept: A collaborative shared office linking Otemachi and the world

Global Business Hub Tokyo calls itself “a collaborative shared office linking Otemachi and the world”. Run by Mitsubishi Estate, it brings together companies entering Japan from overseas and companies growing towards global markets.
Offices come furnished, with electricity and internet included. Being able to move in in as little as two weeks is a big advantage for companies arriving from abroad, the website says.
steps: There are 50 furnished offices for 2–20 people, with electricity and internet included.
You can start in as little as two weeks — ideal for companies that need a base in Japan quickly.
There are 14 meeting rooms for 4–20 people.
With many meeting rooms for the number of tenants, finding a room for a meeting is rarely a problem.
Seminars and launches for up to 200
The event space holds up to 200 people for seminars and product launches.
It sits on the same floor as a place for tenants to connect with each other and with people from outside.

word.title: What is a furnished office?
body: An office with desks, chairs and storage already in place, ready to use as soon as the contract is signed. At Global Business Hub Tokyo, electricity and internet are included too.
No choosing furniture, running cables or signing extra contracts. For a company arriving from abroad, this decides whether the first few weeks go into setup or into work.

credits: Global Business Hub Tokyo (Mitsubishi Estate Co., Ltd.)
Global Business Hub Tokyo official website: “Top”

name: EGG
card: Shin-Marunouchi Building 10F — a “360° Innovation Place” for founders
title: EGG — Mitsubishi Estate's incubation office on the 10th and 9th floors of the Shin-Marunouchi Building
lead: Right in front of Tokyo Station, EGG is on the 10th and 9th floors of the Shin-Marunouchi Building, run by Mitsubishi Estate. This incubation office in Marunouchi has private offices, an event space, the Sundial Lounge and an all-day dining room. Its motto is “360° Innovation Place”. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Private offices / event space / Sundial Lounge / all-day dining
concept: 360° Innovation Place

EGG calls itself a “360° Innovation Place” and is run as a community hub where entrepreneurs in Marunouchi move forward together. The website describes it as a combination of refined workspace and an active business network.

It is on the upper floors of the Shin-Marunouchi Building, facing the Marunouchi exit of Tokyo Station. Reception is on the 10th floor. Private offices, shared spaces and a place to eat are all in one facility.
steps: The shared lounge where members gather
The Sundial Lounge is the members' shared lounge, for work, meetings and breaks.
From the upper floors of the Shin-Marunouchi Building, it looks out over Marunouchi.
Private offices are rooms for teams. Entrepreneurs who want a base in Marunouchi and companies arriving from overseas move in here.
Members move between the shared lounge and their own rooms as they work.
A place to gather, and lunch
The event space hosts gatherings for members and people from outside.
The all-day dining room is open 12:00–17:00, and mealtimes double as time for members to meet.

word.title: What is an incubation office?
body: An office for growing newly founded companies and new businesses. Besides renting rooms, it provides connections and support programmes.
EGG plays this role in the middle of Marunouchi, one of Japan's leading business districts. Having large corporations in the building next door is a value that sites in other areas cannot offer.

name: X-NIHONBASHI TOWER
card: A hub for space-business collaboration on the 7th floor of Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower
title: X-NIHONBASHI TOWER — Mitsui Fudosan's hub for the space business, on the 7th floor of Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower
lead: X-NIHONBASHI TOWER is on the 7th floor of Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower, directly connected to Mitsukoshimae Station. It is one of the sites of X-NIHONBASHI (pronounced “Cross Nihonbashi”), Mitsui Fudosan's hub for collaboration in the space business, with coworking, conference and meeting space in 307 m². To use it, you need to join the general incorporated association Cross U. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: About 120 theatre-style / about 40 coworking seats / about 150 standing
hero_cap: The coworking and conference space at X-NIHONBASHI TOWER
concept: Towards new innovation, in space and on Earth

X-NIHONBASHI is a stage where people gather and connect to grow the space business and create new innovation in space and on the ground. Run by Mitsui Fudosan, it has two facilities: TOWER in Nihonbashi Mitsui Tower and BASE in the Nihonbashi IT Building.
TOWER uses a single 307 m² room for coworking, conferences and meetings: about 120 seats theatre-style, about 40 as coworking, or about 150 standing. The same room changes shape to fit the use.
steps: As a coworking space it has about 40 seats, open 8:00–19:00 on weekdays.
Membership of Cross U is required — a focused place where people in the space business gather.
For conferences it seats about 120 theatre-style or holds about 150 standing.
Space-business presentations and networking events take place in the same room as the coworking — a place to work and a place to present, in one.
Floors 3–4 of the Nihonbashi IT Building

X-NIHONBASHI BASE is on the 3rd and 4th floors of the Nihonbashi IT Building, a one-minute walk from Mitsukoshimae Station. It has coworking, a conference room, a bar lounge, meeting rooms, an exhibition area, web-meeting booths and solo work booths.
Members can use TOWER and BASE as two bases within Nihonbashi.

word.title: What is Cross U?
body: The general incorporated association you must join to use the X-NIHONBASHI facilities — a body bringing together companies and people involved in the space business.
Limiting use to members means the person at the next seat works in the same field. That is the strength of a coworking space with a clear focus.

name: POTLUCK YAESU
card: A lounge connecting Japan's regions with Tokyo, on the 5th floor of Tokyo Midtown Yaesu
title: POTLUCK YAESU — an innovation field where regional dreams gather, on the 5th floor of Tokyo Midtown Yaesu
lead: Innovation Field Yaesu is on the 5th floor of Tokyo Midtown Yaesu, in front of the Yaesu exit of Tokyo Station. It is the base of POTLUCK YAESU, a project for regional economies planned and run jointly by Mitsui Fudosan and NewsPicks Re:gion, with a café, a lounge, a studio for about 140 people and an exhibition area. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Café & kitchen / lounge / studio & event space (about 140) / exhibition
Mitsui Fudosan and NewsPicks Re:gion (joint planning and operation)
hero_cap: The lounge at Innovation Field Yaesu
concept: Where Japan's dreams gather — and grow into the world's

POTLUCK YAESU calls itself “Japan Presentation Field — where Japan's dreams gather and grow into the world's”. True to the name, a potluck meal, it is where businesses and people brought from regions all over Japan meet in front of Tokyo Station.

It is planned and run jointly by Mitsui Fudosan and NewsPicks Re:gion. Eating, talking, showing and presenting: four places on one floor create a flow where people from the regions and from Tokyo mix.
steps: The lounge is open 11:00–22:00 on weekdays and 11:00–19:00 on weekends and holidays.
Right in front of Tokyo Station, it is easy to drop by between business trips and trains.
The café and kitchen is Chikaba Kitchen Tokyo Yaesu, open 11:00–20:00 on weekdays and 11:00–18:00 on weekends and holidays.
Regional ingredients and dishes become the first point of contact with people in Tokyo.
A stage for 140, and a place to show
The studio and event space holds about 140 people for presentations of regional businesses and networking events.
The exhibition area shows regional products and initiatives. Hear the story, see the product, taste it — all on one floor.

word.title: What is a potluck?
body: A meal where every guest brings a dish to share. POTLUCK YAESU takes its name from the word.
Regions across Japan bring their businesses and people and lay them on the table in front of Tokyo Station — on the 5th floor of Tokyo Midtown Yaesu, the place lives up to its name.

credits: POTLUCK YAESU (Mitsui Fudosan Co., Ltd. / NewsPicks Re:gion)

name: MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama
card: Seven floors of a Showa-era building: café, print studio, gallery and a rooftop garden
title: MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama — coworking, a studio and a gallery on seven floors of a Showa-era building in Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho
lead: MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama is in Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho, in the Bakuro-yokoyama district between the Kanda and Sumida rivers. It uses seven floors of a Showa-era building: a coffee shop and an upcycling studio on the ground floor, workspaces on floors 2–4, a gallery on the 7th and a permaculture garden on the roof. Three nearby stations are each a two-minute walk away. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1F café & studio / 2–4F workspace / 5–6F private rooms / 7F gallery / rooftop garden
hero_cap: MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama, using a whole Showa-era building
concept: Working, making and showing, layered in a Showa-era building

MIDORI.so is a coworking community exploring “the future of work in a society that values the individual”. The Bakuro-yokoyama site sits in a district of wholesalers between the Kanda and Sumida rivers, using seven floors of a building from the Showa era.

There is a coffee shop and an upcycling studio on the ground floor, workspaces and a lounge on floors 2–4, private rooms on the 5th and 6th, a gallery on the 7th and a permaculture garden on the roof — places to work, make and show, stacked in one building.
steps: The second floor has a workspace, lounge and kitchen. Workspaces and meeting rooms continue on the 3rd and 4th floors.
A free desk is ¥42,350 a month and a fixed desk ¥60,500 (both with an ¥11,000 sign-up fee). Pop-in is ¥2,200 a day or ¥22,000 for an 11-day pack.
An upcycling studio with Risograph printing
The ground-floor studio has Risograph, inkjet and painting equipment, so ideas from the workspace upstairs can be made real downstairs.
There is also a coffee shop on the ground floor — the doorway through which neighbours come into the building.
The Risograph in the ground-floor studio
An exhibition space from ¥33,000 a day
The 7th floor is a gallery. The basic rate is ¥33,000 a day; creators can exhibit for a week for ¥110,000.
Bakuro-yokoyama, Higashi-Nihonbashi and Bakurocho stations are each a two-minute walk away.

word.title: What is permaculture?
body: An approach to designing lasting ways of living and growing food by following natural systems. MIDORI.so Bakuroyokoyama has a permaculture garden on its roof.
Few coworking spaces have a garden on the roof. People who work at desks can spend time with their hands in the soil without leaving the building.
